content.content: A node set member is a change that owns its own node document: the path `nodes/<its own change id>.json` is present at the change the id names (D1b, xwyryumr; S2-path, pumpuqkv). The set is the ids of exactly those changes, taken from jj's change listing — a candidate listing of the changes touching `nodes/` (e.g. `jj log -r 'files("nodes/")'`), each candidate kept only where the change's own document is there — never from listing the working copy's `nodes/` directory.
content.rationale: Touching `nodes/` is not owning a node. A node's id is the id of the change that owns it (D1b, xwyryumr), so the set is a set of change ids, and jj is what reports changes — the enumeration crosses the jj seam through M-jj (zruxtxrv), running its own scoped change listing rather than mapping a fixed command. Drawing the set from the read's own source keeps the two in agreement: S2-read (nqktpzuu) reads a document from the change that owns it, and a set taken from anywhere else could list nodes the read cannot reach, or miss nodes it can. The candidate listing is the changes touching `nodes/`, which is a superset of the changes that own their own document: a buffer that edits a sibling's document, or a stray file left under the directory, touches the path while carrying no `nodes/<its own id>.json`, and is listed under an id that names no document — taking the listing as the set names changes the read cannot reach, the missing document the set then surfaces. S2-path (pumpuqkv) fixes the scoping: a node is `nodes/<id>.json` and D1b makes the id the owning change's, so a change is a node exactly when its own document is present at the change the id names, and a change that carries no node document of its own is not one — jj's root sentinel names no file, and the empty working-copy tip owns no node. A directory listing instead reads the working copy, which materialises only the nodes present at its own revision: when the working copy sits earlier in history, a node recorded later in the stack is invisible, so the set is silently partial — the same defect S2-read names for the read. A file listing at the working-copy revision (`jj file list`) answers a tree rather than the graph and inherits that same partiality.
